confidence_note: the signup credit, its 12-month expiry, the no-card statement and the per-result price are quoted from first-party documentation; no keyed search was made, so the read path is unprobed; a keyed call that returns results would raise it to measured

free_tier.stated: USD 10 of free credits on signup, USD 20 with a company email, no card; the free credits expire 12 months after signup
free_tier.notes: Search is billed per result returned, not per request: a 10-result web search is 1 credit, and pay-as-you-go buys 1,600 credits per USD 10. The nearest metered_on term is request-count; the true basis is the count of results returned.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a search result

retention.stated: one-time signup credit; it expires 12 months after signup and does not renew

interface_detail: POST https://api.valyu.ai/v1/search with an x-api-key header; Contents, Answer and DeepResearch endpoints draw on the same key and balance; a hosted MCP server is offered
tooling: Python SDK (pip install valyu), TypeScript SDK (valyu-js), Rust SDK, a CLI and a hosted MCP server
chaining: A bounded search leg whose one key also reaches SEC filings, arXiv, PubMed, patents and clinical trials, priced per result; the signup balance is spent once, so it suits a finite job rather than a standing crawl

limits.value: USD 10 one-time (USD 20 with a company email), about 1,600 ten-result web searches at 1 credit each; a request the balance cannot cover answers 402 and nothing is billed as overage
5 search requests a second on the Pay-as-you-go plan, per the documented 429 example; limits are per organisation and per endpoint, with no daily quota

binding_note: the one-time signup balance is exhausted long before the 5-a-second rate limit is reached

identity_cost.detail: signup by email, Google or GitHub with no card; a company email doubles the signup credit to USD 20

reliability_note: a keyless GET to /v1/search answered 403 with a missing-token message, so there is no anonymous route; no throttle or ban event recorded
